NetPilot has no analytics, no ads, no trackers and no telemetry. Profiles are stored in the app\u2019s private storage and excluded from platform backups. The only network traffic the app itself generates is DNS resolution and your own VPN tunnels. The full source is in the repository for you to verify.

NetPilot\u2019s runtime code uses only first-party Android libraries. The projects below are used by the build & test tooling, or are the platform libraries this app is built on. We are grateful to their authors.

Built for Android TV first — works on phones and tablets too.

Android protects system settings: no app — including this one — can change Private DNS on its own. The standard, root-free way is to grant one permission over ADB. It takes about two minutes and survives reboots and app updates.
1. On the TV/phone: enable Developer options, then turn on \u201CUSB debugging\u201D (on Android TV it is \u201CNetwork debugging\u201D — note the IP:port shown).
2. On your computer with adb installed, connect: adb connect <TV-IP>:5555 (phones: plug in USB instead).
4. Press \u201CI granted it\u201D below — NetPilot verifies instantly. You never need to do this again.

No computer? Two options: (1) use Zero-setup Secure DNS above — one tap, no ADB at all; or (2) install Termux on any Android phone (F-Droid), run “pkg install android-tools”, then “adb connect <TV-IP>:5555” and run the grant command from the phone over Wi-Fi. Some TV launchers hide the Private DNS UI entirely — that is why NetPilot exists: the feature works, only the menu is missing.
